_source: Methodology development process for Git Hub.pdf — Tables 2 and 3. All names and descriptions are verbatim from the PDF.

ipcc_sectors.name: Energy
ipcc_sectors.description: Fuel combustion activities including electricity and heat production, petroleum refining, manufacturing and construction industries. Fugitive emissions from solid fuels, oil, and natural gas systems. This sector covers all greenhouse gas emissions from the combustion of fossil fuels and fugitive emissions from fuel production, processing, storage, transmission, and distribution. Includes power generation, district heating, industrial energy use, commercial and residential energy consumption, and energy transformation.

ipcc_sectors.name: Transport
ipcc_sectors.description: All greenhouse gas emissions from the combustion of fuel for transportation activities including road transportation (cars, trucks, buses, motorcycles), railways, domestic aviation, domestic navigation and shipping, pipeline transport, and off-road transport. Covers both passenger and freight transport. This is reported as a sub-category of Energy in GHG inventories but tracked separately for policy measures due to its distinct policy interventions (vehicle standards, modal shift, electrification, sustainable fuels).

ipcc_sectors.name: Industrial processes and product use
ipcc_sectors.description: Greenhouse gas emissions from industrial processes that chemically or physically transform materials, and from the use of products. Includes mineral industry emissions (cement, lime, glass), chemical industry emissions (ammonia, nitric acid, carbide), metal industry emissions (iron, steel, aluminium), emissions from non-energy use of fuels and solvent use, electronics industry emissions, use of fluorinated substitutes for ozone depleting substances (HFCs, PFCs, SF6), and other product manufacture and use.

ipcc_sectors.name: Agriculture
ipcc_sectors.description: Non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions from agricultural activities including enteric fermentation from livestock, livestock manure management, rice cultivation, agricultural soils (direct and indirect N2O emissions from managed soils, including synthetic fertilizers, animal manure applied to soils, crop residues, and cultivation of organic soils), prescribed burning of savannas, field burning of agricultural residues, and other agricultural activities. Covers crop production, animal husbandry, and associated land management practices.

ipcc_sectors.name: Land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF)
ipcc_sectors.description: Greenhouse gas emissions and removals from land use, land-use change and forestry activities. Covers six land-use categories: forest land, cropland, grassland, wetlands, settlements, and other land. Includes carbon stock changes in living biomass, dead organic matter, and soils. Covers afforestation, reforestation, deforestation, forest management, cropland management, grazing land management, and revegetation. Also includes harvested wood products and natural disturbances on managed land.

ipcc_sectors.name: Waste
ipcc_sectors.description: Greenhouse gas emissions from waste management and disposal activities including solid waste disposal on land (managed and unmanaged landfills, open dumps), biological treatment of solid waste (composting, anaerobic digestion), incineration and open burning of waste, and wastewater treatment and discharge (domestic, commercial, and industrial wastewater). Covers both municipal and industrial waste streams, sanitation infrastructure, and sewage systems.

ipcc_sectors.name: Other / Cross-cutting
ipcc_sectors.description: Activities, policies and measures that span multiple IPCC sectors or do not fit neatly into a single sector category. This includes cross-cutting policy frameworks, institutional capacity building, education and awareness, gender mainstreaming, finance mechanisms, monitoring and reporting systems, and multi-sectoral strategies. Also used for water and sanitation infrastructure, health-related climate measures, and other activities not captured by the six main IPCC sectors.

nbs_categories.name: Protection, management, and restoration of marine and coastal habitats
nbs_categories.description: This includes coastal zone risk retention, living shorelines, tidal basins, oyster beds, artificial reefs, tidal salt marshes, sustainable coastal management, marine production promotion, coastal environment monitoring and risk assessment, disease management of marine resources, mangrove protection, coral reef protection, seagrass protection, marine protected areas, restoring marine ecosystems, coastal wetland, seagrass, coral reef and mangrove restoration, sustainable fishery, marine ecosystem service management, tidal salt marshes, restoration of seagrass beds, mangroves, terrestrial.

nbs_categories.name: Agriculture and livestock management
nbs_categories.description: This includes terrestrial ecosystems, climate-resilient crops, climate-resilient livestock management, climate-smart agriculture, parametric insurance, regenerative agriculture, agroecology, crop diversification, community-seeds banks, integrated water management, grazing land management, manure management, agricultural land and soil management, agriculture and livestock disease management, sustainable agricultural education and consulting, agroforestry, agricultural diversification, improved grazing land management, reduced grassland conversion to cropland, sustainable rangeland management, sustainable land management, sustainable grazing, optimal grazing intensity, conservation agriculture, landscape restoration, nature-positive dietary changes, reducing food waste, reducing post-harvest losses, sustainable sourcing and use of resources, supply-chain diversification, improved food processing and retailing, improved energy use in food systems, reducing food loss, and improved supply chain resilience.

nbs_categories.name: Water management
nbs_categories.description: This includes catchment protection, sustainable irrigation, watershed restoration, freshwater ecosystem restoration, integrated water resource management, water management systems, securing water quality, water education and consulting, monitoring of water resources, service management of water ecosystems, and pluvial flood risk reduction.

nbs_categories.name: Forest management, restoration, and protection
nbs_categories.description: This includes natural forest management, improved plantations, sustainable forestry practices, preventing illegal logging, reducing deforestation and forest degradation, fire management, REDD+, reforestation, afforestation, tree planting on degraded land, temperate and tropical forest restoration, forest carbon sink management, and monitoring forest changes.

nbs_categories.name: Protection and restoration of wetlands and freshwater ecosystems
nbs_categories.description: This includes river, inland water and wetland protection, peatland rewetting, avoiding peat impacts, freshwater ecosystem protection, wetland management, service management of freshwater ecosystems, peatland restoration, dune restoration, freshwater ecosystem restoration, catchment restoration, watershed protection, restoration and reduced conversion of coastal wetlands, restoration and reduced conversion of peatlands, sustainable fishery, and restoring peatlands.

nbs_categories.name: Ecosystem protection and connectivity
nbs_categories.description: This includes establishing protected areas, community reserves, wildlife corridors, restore pollinator habitats, prevent species extinction, habitat rewilding, restricting invasive species and pests, ecosystem change detection, other effective conservation measures (OECM), and increased connectivity between protected areas.

nbs_categories.name: Soil fertility management and restoration
nbs_categories.description: This includes increased soil organic carbon, reduced soil erosion, reduced soil salinization, reduced soil compaction, conservation tillage, biochar application, improved cropland soil management, soil restoration, soil improvement, and sustainable intensification.

nbs_categories.name: Nature-based risk management and disaster prevention
nbs_categories.description: This includes agricultural disaster management and invasive alien species and pest control, disease surveillance, wildfire management, fire management, flood control, infrastructure and critical systems resilience, reduced landslides and hazards, making human settlement safer, environmental risk monitoring, forecasting and warning systems, resource-based early warnings, reduced pollution, acidification prevention, disaster risk reduction and management in agriculture, security and diversification in critical sectors such as energy, food and water, risk sharing instruments and insurance, livelihood diversification, and management of urban sprawl (blue and green spaces).

nbs_categories.name: Nature-based carbon sequestration
nbs_categories.description: This includes Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS), enhanced weathering of minerals, tree planting for carbon sequestration, afforestation, reforestation, proforestation, tree intercropping, silvopasture, restore forests for carbon sequestration, and improved plantations for carbon storage.

nbs_categories.name: Urban settlements management
nbs_categories.description: This includes urban green spaces, sponge city, urban forests, green roofs, green walls, urban wetlands, rain gardens, vegetated stormwater systems, green infrastructure, urban farms.

globe_categories.name: Access and benefit sharing
globe_categories.description: Access to genetic resources, with a focus on prior informed consent, and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits of genetic diversity with those whose knowledge is used, on Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT) and taking into account all rights over those resources, and by appropriate funding. Actions can include: Bioprospecting/screening for biodiversity areas and establishing permitting processes: regulating the screening for biodiversity areas and resources for commercial use and all processes that allow this research. Contractual arrangements: arrangements between genetic resource (knowledge) provider and user, the provider and the state as well as the user and the state that ensure legal certainty and transparency about access to genetic resources, the involvement of the local population, allow for research, as well as how the financial and non-financial benefit of the use is shared. Benefit-sharing mechanism: the commitment to channel a fair share of the benefits for the use of genetic resources, whether monetary or non-monetary, back to the range of designated participants. Nagoya Protocol: institutional structures of the protocol, and expenditures related explicitly to the ratification and Nagoya-specific processes (e.g. designation of a national focal point, ABS clearing house mechanism), in addition to capacity-building and awareness raising.

globe_categories.name: Biodiversity awareness and knowledge
globe_categories.description: Biodiversity awareness and knowledge includes a wide range of different topics. Biodiversity knowledge aims to produce, generate and provide an easy and timely access to quality data and information, to support all efforts in halting biodiversity loss or maintaining and increasing current biodiversity levels. Knowledge generation and distribution includes formal and non-formal contexts, technical training, biodiversity communication and scientific research, the indigenous and local communities' knowledge. Actions can include: Formal education: integration of biodiversity into hierarchically structured, chronologically graded educational system running from primary through the tertiary institutions. Non-formal and informal biodiversity education: planned, structured programmes and processes outside the formal educational curriculum, designed to improve a range of skills and competencies related to biodiversity and the KMGBF and shift individual acquires attitudes and values. Biodiversity awareness and communication: efforts to bring public awareness to issues relating to biodiversity to the attention of key groups who have the power to influence outcomes, including campaigns, surveys, events, and establishment of physical spaces. Biodiversity scientific research: includes assessments and studies undertaken on a systematic basis in order to increase the stock of knowledge on biodiversity, methods to collect, process, and exchange biodiversity data, citizen science and community and indigenous-lead knowledge creation. Indigenous and local communities knowledge: promotion, protection, and utilization of knowledge, innovations and practices of indigenous and local communities for biodiversity decision-making, with FPIC.

globe_categories.name: Biosafety
globe_categories.description: Includes two sub-categories: (1) Prevention, containment, and eradication of invasive alien species (IAS) and (2) safe handling, transport and use of living modified organisms (LMOs/GMOs) resulting from modern biotechnology that may have adverse effects on biological diversity. Actions include: Identification and prioritization of IAS species, their introduction pathways and most effective measures to avoid direct or indirect introduction and their impacts. Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs), including Living modified organisms (LMO): standards and regulation to ensure the precautionary principle before introducing modified species, research, biosafety evaluation, and capacity building on impacts of GMOs, and compliance to international and regional and sub-regional agreements on Biosafety, in particular the Cartagena Protocol.

globe_categories.name: Green economy
globe_categories.description: A green economy results in improved human well-being and social equity, while significantly reducing environmental risks and ecological scarcities and can be considered as one that is low in carbon, resource efficient, and socially inclusive. Actions include: Green supply chain: establishing a green supply chain that integrates environmentally responsible practices related to sourcing, product design, manufacturing, packaging, logistics and end-of-life product management. Reduction of harm to biodiversity in extractive industries: disclosure of environmental impact by extractive activities and mitigation measures taken. Sustainable consumption: reduction of negative impact on biodiversity by improving the ecological footprint, reducing per-capita consumption, avoiding waste and overexploitation. Sustainable energy: reduction of negative impacts of energy production, transmission and distribution, innovative energy systems not harming (or even supporting) biodiversity conservation. Sustainable tourism: tourism that takes full account of its current and future economic, social and environmental impacts, addressing the needs of visitors, the industry, the environment and host communities. Sustainable transportation: reducing the negative impacts by reducing the reliance on natural resources, providing environmentally friendly alternatives and increasing public transport. Sustainable urban and rural areas: environmental impact assessments of infrastructure projects, improving water quality, and disaster risk reduction.

globe_categories.name: Biodiversity planning and finance
globe_categories.description: National, state or local planning, policy, finance, legal, coordination and enforcement actions crosscutting in nature that cover multiple biodiversity categories or general issues, such as biodiversity planning and policy. Activities include: Biodiversity laws, policies, and plans: change, creation and implementation of biodiversity laws, policies, and plans, harmonization of standards and disclosure by companies and public projects, measures to safeguard biodiversity and ecosystem services by financial institutions, business, public institutions and other relevant actors. Policy coherence: policy coherence and mainstreaming to include biodiversity relevant aspects in all other sector's plans, policies, regulations and decision-making processes. Biodiversity coordination and management: includes the update of NBSAPs including all stakeholders, indigenous peoples, local communities, and women, science-based monitoring and evaluation for adaptive management. Biodiversity finance planning and coordination: measures to increase domestic and international finance flows to biodiversity, by introducing new instruments and mechanisms, improving the spending of currently available funds. Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Framework: formal, systematic process to analyse and address the environmental effects of policies, plans and programmes. Spatial planning: developing spatial data and spatial arrangements of all kinds of territories. Multi-lateral environmental agreements: ratification, implementation and monitoring of relevant conventions including CBD and its protocols, CITES, CMS, ITPGRFA, Ramsar Convention, WHC, High Seas Treaty, IPPC, and regional conventions.

globe_categories.name: Pollution management
globe_categories.description: Pollution is the introduction of harmful materials (i.e. pollutants) into the environment at a faster rate than can be dispersed, diluted, decomposed, recycled, or stored in some harmless form. Biodiversity benefits from its management, consisting of pollution prevention at the source, reduction, reusing, recycling, treatment or disposal. Activities can include: Protection and remediation of soil, groundwater and surface water: measures aimed at the prevention of pollutant infiltration, cleaning up of soils and water bodies and the protection of soil from erosion and other physical degradation as well as from salinisation. Protection of ambient air and climate: activities aimed at the reduction of emissions into the ambient air or ambient concentrations of air pollutants as well as measures aimed at the control of emissions of greenhouse gases. Waste management: reduced/avoided pollution by managing all kinds of waste, including wastewater. Coastal and marine pollution debris management: reduced/avoided coastal and marine pollution debris with activities tackling land- and sea-based sources, focusing especially on plastic. Other pollution management measures: noise, vibration, light, temperature, radiation, pharmaceutical, heavy metals, Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs), Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCB).

globe_categories.name: Protected areas and other conservation measures
globe_categories.description: In situ and ex situ measures to protect and safeguard biodiversity at genetic, species and ecosystem levels. The effort can be area-based through protected areas, their expansion, connection or buffer zones; but also includes other conservation measures, e.g. focusing on specific species or establishing other effective conservation measures. Activities can include: Management and expansion of Protected Areas, including Indigenous and Communities Conserved Areas (ICCA): maintaining or establishing protected areas designated or regulated and managed to achieve specific conservation objectives, including all IUCN Categories (Ia-VI). Management of areas outside of Protected Areas: activities to manage, protect and develop transboundary areas, biodiversity corridors, Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs), landscapes and seascapes. Other effective area-based conservation measures (OECM): governance and management of areas outside of Protected Areas in ways that achieve positive and sustained long-term outcomes for the in situ conservation of biodiversity. Conservation of species: targeted protection of species, in particular wildlife and migratory species, within or outside of protected and conserved areas, including reducing threats such as overconsumption, trade and poaching, climate change, displacement, reduced habitats, and Invasive Alien Species.

globe_categories.name: Restoration
globe_categories.description: Ecosystem restoration means assisting in the recovery of ecosystems that have been degraded or destroyed, as well as conserving the ecosystems that are still intact. It should result in a rehabilitation of the ecosystem functions and services. Restoration efforts are recognized to support the achievement of all Rio Conventions (CBD, UNCCD, UNFCCC) as well as the SDGs. Activities can include: Reintroduction and translocation of species: capture, transport and release or introduction of species, habitats or other ecological material from one location to another to support habitat or species restoration. Site redevelopment and engineering: efforts to prevent ecosystem degradation and repair damage already caused, for example by removing drivers of degradation, clean up after chemical or physical damage, and restoration of river channels. Site management: ongoing management or maintenance of restoration sites after the restoration activity has been realized to ensure the continuity of the initiated trajectory or status quo, including management planning, awareness raising on restoration, and landscape care and maintenance.

globe_categories.name: Sustainable use
globe_categories.description: Sustainable Use is the use of components of biological diversity in a way and at a rate that does not lead to the long-term decline of biological diversity, thereby maintaining its potential to meet the needs and aspirations of present and future generations. This category is distinguished from the green economy by its focus on ecosystem services, primarily production and the underlying support services. Activities include: Agrobiodiversity: agricultural biodiversity including inventory, surveys and statistics of genetic variety, on-farm conservation, seed banks, incentives for sustainable plantation of local and traditional varieties, and the ITPGRFA. Sustainable Agriculture: combining environmental protection, production and social equity in food production. Sustainable aquaculture: controlled cultivation of fish, shellfish, and aquatic plants reducing environmental harm. Sustainable fisheries: combating overfishing, ensuring habitat protection, and use of non-aggressive fishing devices. Sustainable forestry: combining environmental protection, production and social equity while safeguarding biodiversity. Sustainable freshwater: reducing overuse of freshwater resources and other threats to the freshwater ecosystem. Sustainable marine and coastal management: combining environmental protection, production and social equity. Sustainable rangelands: combining environmental protection for wildlife, habitats and watersheds with production and social equity. Sustainable wildlife: ensuring all uses of wildlife (fishing, gathering, logging, terrestrial animal harvesting) are done within ecological limits.

globe_subcategories.name: Screening for biodiversity areas and establishing permitting processes
globe_subcategories.description: Regulating the screening (bioprospecting) for biodiversity areas and resources for commercial use, and all processes that allow this research. Includes issuing permits, oversight of screening activities, and supporting legal frameworks.

globe_subcategories.name: Contractual arrangements
globe_subcategories.description: Contractual arrangements between the genetic resource (or knowledge) provider and user, the provider and the state, and the user and the state. These ensure legal certainty and transparency on access to genetic resources, involvement of local populations, provisions for research, and how financial and non-financial benefits are shared. Includes compliance support.

globe_subcategories.name: Benefit-sharing mechanism
globe_subcategories.description: Mechanisms committed to channel a fair share of the benefits for the use of genetic resources, monetary or non-monetary, back to providers. Includes up-front or milestone payments, royalties, contributions to biodiversity funds, collaborative research funding, joint ventures, IP rights sharing, venture capital, capacity-building, technology transfer, and financial support to provider institutions.

globe_subcategories.name: Nagoya Protocol (ratified/enforced)
globe_subcategories.description: Institutional structures of the Nagoya Protocol, including expenditures for ratification, designation of a national focal point, the ABS clearing house mechanism, and Nagoya-specific processes. Also includes capacity-building and awareness raising about the Protocol. Implementation of ABS-related legislation falls under other subcategories.

globe_subcategories.name: Access to resources, information and decision-making
globe_subcategories.description: Financial and non-financial resources directed to rights- and stakeholders (especially Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities, women, and youth), including access to complete and accurate information, and their involvement as key partners in decision-making, including Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC).

globe_subcategories.name: Formal biodiversity education
globe_subcategories.description: Learning in organized, structured environments within the educational system, from primary school through higher education, and including specialized programmes and institutions for full-time technical and professional training. Covers general biodiversity topics and specific ones like biodiversity finance. Excludes non-school offers (see 2.02).

globe_subcategories.name: Non-formal biodiversity education and technical training
globe_subcategories.description: Planned, structured programmes and processes of personal and social education outside the formal educational system, designed to improve skills and competencies. Includes vocational training outside universities, informal education through daily experience, on-the-job learning, community-based learning, conferences, South-South knowledge transfer.

globe_subcategories.name: Biodiversity awareness and communication
globe_subcategories.description: Efforts to bring biodiversity issues to the attention of key groups (public awareness campaigns, surveys, events, establishment of physical spaces). Governments use communication as an instrument to support biodiversity conservation, address economic constraints, motivate action, and inform audiences about policies and legislation.

globe_subcategories.name: Biodiversity scientific research
globe_subcategories.description: All types of research to increase the stock of knowledge and statistical data about biodiversity, from very basic to concrete application, including digital approaches and valuation of biodiversity, by civil, private, public, or scholar actors. Includes methods to collect, process, and exchange biodiversity data; citizen science; and community and indigenous-led knowledge creation.

globe_subcategories.name: Indigenous Peoples' and local communities' knowledge
globe_subcategories.description: Promotion, protection and utilization of knowledge, innovations and practices of Indigenous Peoples and local communities developed from experience gained over centuries and adapted to local culture and environment. Includes documentation and analysis of traditional knowledge (stories, songs, folklore, proverbs, cultural values, beliefs, rituals, community laws, agricultural practices) to enhance education, research, and raise awareness.

globe_subcategories.name: CBD clearing-house mechanism
globe_subcategories.description: The mission of the CBD clearing house mechanism: information services and other means to promote and facilitate scientific and technical cooperation, knowledge sharing and information exchange, and to establish a fully operational network of Parties and partners.

globe_subcategories.name: Invasive Alien Species (IAS)
globe_subcategories.description: Identification and prioritization of (potential) IAS and their entry points; regular assessment of current status; measures to prevent their entry, spread and establishment; their removal, eradication, or at least containment; and cross-cutting activities such as awareness raising, training, regional cooperation, and adoption of relevant legislation. Note: domestic animals (cats, dogs) causing similar negative impact on wildlife can be classified here if the purpose is documented.

globe_subcategories.name: Genetically modified organisms (GMOs) and Living modified organisms (LMOs)
globe_subcategories.description: Standards and regulation ensuring the precautionary principle before introducing modified species. Research, biosafety evaluation, capacity building on GMO/LMO impacts, monitoring of GMO procedures, and compliance with the Cartagena Protocol and other biosafety agreements.

globe_subcategories.name: Green supply chain
globe_subcategories.description: Establishing a green supply chain that integrates environmentally responsible practices related to sourcing, product design, manufacturing, packaging, logistics, and end-of-life product management. Improving efficiency; reducing emissions, resource use, and waste.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable extractive industries
globe_subcategories.description: Recovery and processing of raw materials (fossil fuels, minerals, aggregates like sand, gravel, clay). Disclosure of environmental impact by extractive activities and mitigation measures. Ensuring biodiversity impact is avoided or minimized. In resource-dependent countries, profits can be channeled to biodiversity-friendly investments.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable consumption
globe_subcategories.description: Reducing negative impact on biodiversity by improving the ecological footprint, reducing per-capita consumption, and avoiding waste and overexploitation. Divided into: Food & Nutrition; Construction & Housing; Mobility; Working and Office; Leisure & Tourism; Textile & Clothing.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable energy
globe_subcategories.description: Energy production using sources that can be used repeatedly without depletion; decreasing overall energy need by changing to alternatives; increasing energy efficiency. Reducing negative impacts of energy production, transmission and distribution, and innovative energy systems not harming (or even supporting) biodiversity.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable tourism
globe_subcategories.description: Tourism that fully accounts for current and future economic, social and environmental impacts, addressing needs of visitors, the industry, the environment, and host communities. Includes government roles: marketing and promotion; border security; aviation regulation; planning regulations; control or management of tourism attractions (e.g. national parks); skills development; road infrastructure.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable transportation
globe_subcategories.description: Reducing negative impacts of transportation by reducing reliance on natural resources, providing environmentally friendly alternatives, and increasing public transport.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable urban and rural areas
globe_subcategories.description: Environmental impact assessments of infrastructure projects, improving water quality, disaster risk reduction, and integrated planning for urban and rural areas that considers biodiversity. Green infrastructure, urban biodiversity, rural livelihoods.

globe_subcategories.name: Biodiversity laws, policies, plans
globe_subcategories.description: Legal action at every level of government (national, state or local) whose main objective is to address biodiversity directly, such as to conserve/restore biodiversity (e.g. establishment of new Protected Areas), or to address the causes for biodiversity loss (e.g. incentives for public, private, civil actors). Includes criminal persecution for breaching these laws. Implementation or execution of the law is classified under the relevant subcategories.

globe_subcategories.name: Other relevant laws, policies, plans
globe_subcategories.description: Legal action at every level of government that addresses biodiversity indirectly by focusing on non-biodiversity sectors. Legislation can be relevant by including biodiversity safeguards in laws focused on other topics (e.g. green economy) or by increasing policy coherence. Particularly relevant for mainstreaming and a whole-of-government approach.

globe_subcategories.name: Biodiversity coordination and management
globe_subcategories.description: Coordination with different stakeholders and rightsholders at local, national or international level, where the state participates or provides a framework/platform. Includes update of NBSAPs, stakeholder engagement (Indigenous peoples, local communities, women), science-based monitoring and evaluation for adaptive management.

globe_subcategories.name: Biodiversity finance
globe_subcategories.description: All types of measures to increase domestic and international finance flows to biodiversity, by introducing new instruments and mechanisms, improving the spending of currently available funds, and providing legal frameworks for non-public actors.

globe_subcategories.name: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Framework
globe_subcategories.description: A formal, systematic process to analyse and address the environmental effects of policies, plans and programmes and other strategic initiatives. Usually applied at an early stage of decision-making; other aspects (e.g. social considerations) can be included. Note: project-level Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) are classified under the relevant project subcategory, typically under Category 4 Green Economy.

globe_subcategories.name: Spatial planning
globe_subcategories.description: Spatial planning of any territory in a rational way, by coordinating the different interests (production, livelihood, biodiversity conservation, historical/cultural value, recreation, etc.) and sectoral policies. Excludes delineation and zoning in Protected Areas or ICCAs (see 7.01).

globe_subcategories.name: Multilateral Environment Agreement (MEA)
globe_subcategories.description: Actions and steps a government must take to fulfil its obligation as party to environmental agreements. Agreement-specific implementation is assessed in the relevant Primary Biodiversity Categories. The Nagoya Protocol has its own subcategory (1.05).

globe_subcategories.name: Soil and water (protection and remediation)
globe_subcategories.description: Measures aimed at prevention of pollutant infiltration into soil, groundwater and surface water; cleaning up of soils and water bodies; protection of soil from erosion, other physical degradation and salinization.

globe_subcategories.name: Air and atmosphere
globe_subcategories.description: Reduced or avoided pollution to protect ambient air and climate (excluding waste management). Where there are clear stated biodiversity objectives: activities aimed at reduction of emissions into ambient air or ambient concentrations of air pollutants; measures to control emissions of greenhouse gases and gases that adversely affect the stratospheric ozone layer.

globe_subcategories.name: Waste management
globe_subcategories.description: Reduced or avoided pollution by managing all types of waste, including wastewater. Prevention of waste generation; reduction of its harmful effects; collection and treatment of waste (especially recycling and composting); monitoring and regulation; collection and treatment of low-level radioactive waste; street cleaning and collection of public litter.

globe_subcategories.name: Coastal and marine pollution debris management
globe_subcategories.description: Reduced or avoided coastal and marine pollution debris through activities tackling land- and sea-based sources, focusing in particular on plastics.

globe_subcategories.name: Other pollution management measures
globe_subcategories.description: Reduced/avoided pollution in the form of light, noise, vibration, temperature, radiation, Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs), pharmaceutical pollution, PCB oils, heavy metals. Includes supportive actions: research, monitoring, awareness raising, capacity building.

globe_subcategories.name: Management and expansion of protected areas
globe_subcategories.description: Protected Areas (PAs) including Indigenous and Communities Conserved Areas (ICCA). A PA is a geographically defined area designated or regulated and managed to achieve specific conservation objectives, across all IUCN Categories (Ia-VI). Expansion includes analysis of potential areas, identifying management policy considering local ecological and social circumstances, securing land titles, and legal designation.

globe_subcategories.name: Management of areas outside of Protected Areas
globe_subcategories.description: Activities to manage, protect and develop areas outside the PA regime: transboundary areas, biodiversity corridors, Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs), landscapes and seascapes. Includes public and private actor actions and frameworks to maintain, enhance and restore ecological flows, species movement and dynamic processes across intact and fragmented environments outside PAs.

globe_subcategories.name: Other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs)
globe_subcategories.description: Geographically defined areas other than Protected Areas, governed and managed in ways that achieve positive and sustained long-term outcomes for in situ conservation of biodiversity, associated ecosystem functions and services, and where applicable, cultural, spiritual, socio-economic values. Unlike PAs, conservation may not be the primary objective of an OECM yet it delivers effective in-situ biodiversity conservation.

globe_subcategories.name: Conservation of species
globe_subcategories.description: Targeted protection of species, in particular wildlife and migratory species, within or outside of protected and conserved areas. Includes reducing threats such as overconsumption, trade and poaching, climate change, displacement, reduced habitats, and Invasive Alien Species. Includes conservation measures in situ and ex situ.

globe_subcategories.name: Reintroduction and translocation of species
globe_subcategories.description: Reintroduction: introduction into the wild of species from captive stock. Translocation: capture, transport and release or introduction of species, habitats or other ecological material (e.g. soil) from one location to another. Supports habitat or species restoration.

globe_subcategories.name: Site redevelopment and engineering
globe_subcategories.description: Efforts to prevent ecosystem degradation and repair damage already caused, for example by removing drivers of degradation, clean up after chemical or physical damage, and restoration of river channels. Focuses on first steps to initiate restoration (assessing, planning and starting intervention) to remediate damage.

globe_subcategories.name: Site management
globe_subcategories.description: Ongoing management or maintenance of restoration sites after the restoration activity has been realized, to ensure continuity of the initiated trajectory or status quo. Includes management planning, awareness raising on restoration, and landscape care and maintenance.

globe_subcategories.name: Agrobiodiversity
globe_subcategories.description: Management of biological resources important for food and agriculture (genetic resources for food). Covers: harvested crop varieties, livestock breeds, fish species and non-domesticated (wild) resources; non-harvested species supporting food provision (soil micro-biota, pollinators, bees, butterflies, earthworms); non-harvested species in wider environment supporting food production ecosystems. Includes inventory, surveys, on-farm conservation, seed banks, incentives for local and traditional varieties, and ITPGRFA.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable agriculture
globe_subcategories.description: Combining environmental protection, production and related income, and social equity in food production. Practices include organic production, measures to improve soil health and resource efficiency (water saving, changed irrigation, reduced emissions), reduced erosion and reduced commercial pesticide use. May include robots/AI in urban and rural farming. Excludes GMOs (see 3.02). Agroforestry is included here, not in 9.05.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable aquaculture
globe_subcategories.description: Controlled cultivation or farming of fish, shellfish, and aquatic plants aimed at creating a source of aquatic food and products in a way that increases availability while reducing environmental harm and protecting aquatic species. Open-pen aquaculture is currently not considered within GLOBE (due to unavoidable environmental issues).

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable fisheries
globe_subcategories.description: Fishing (removal of aquatic animals from their habitats) that combats overfishing, ensures habitat protection, and uses non-aggressive fishing devices. Covers both lethal fisheries (e.g. traditional commercial) and non-lethal fisheries (e.g. aquarium trade, catch-and-release). Excludes species spending part of their life cycle in terrestrial environments (see 9.09).

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable forestry
globe_subcategories.description: Combining environmental protection, production and related income, and social equity, while safeguarding biodiversity. Considers needs of wildlife and forest ecosystems including abiotic components (soil, water). All human interventions in forests safeguarding biodiversity: avoiding erosion, reducing fire risk, ensuring species survival. Logging within ecological limits, selectively or by clear-cutting small areas, including IPLCs and fair benefit sharing.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable land management
globe_subcategories.description: Sustainable land management aligned with the UNCCD and covering multiple uses. Integrated approaches to land management that prevent degradation and restore ecosystem function, with a focus on preventing desertification.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable marine and coastal management
globe_subcategories.description: Combining environmental protection, production and related income, and social equity for marine and coastal ecosystems. Covers all activities except aquaculture (9.03) and fishery (9.04), including energy generation, shipping, mining, and tourism in marine/coastal areas. Key tools: environmental impact assessments, integrated marine spatial planning, coastal zone management, IPLC inclusion and ownership.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable rangelands
globe_subcategories.description: Sustainable rangeland management combining environmental protection (wildlife, habitats, watersheds), production and related income (livestock, freshwater), and social equity. Considers needs of wildlife and related ecosystems (grassland, shrubland, wetland) and abiotic components (soil, water). All human interventions safeguarding biodiversity: avoiding erosion, reducing fire risk, benefiting from rangeland products and services within ecological limits.

globe_subcategories.name: Sustainable wildlife
globe_subcategories.description: Sustainable management of wildlife: organisms captive or living in the wild that have not been subjected to multigenerational breeding/selection, as well as non-domesticated animals. Covers extractive uses (fishing, gathering, logging, terrestrial animal harvesting) and non-extractive uses (ceremonies, rituals, decorative, energy, food-feed, learning, materials, medicine, recreation). Note: species conservation itself is in 7.04.
